extracted.intended_audience: users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (mathematicians, researchers, and programmers working with polynomial/ideal/module computations)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for SINGULAR functions (Chapter 5): syntax, types, purpose, examples, and notes for using functions that manipulate polynomials, ideals, modules, matrices, and system state.

rubrics_metrics.name: impart
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the imaginary part of a number in a complex ground field; returns 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: impart(number expression). Type: number. Example: ring r=(complex,i),x,dp; impart(1+2*i); → 2. See Section 5.1.129 [repart].

rubrics_metrics.name: indepSet
rubrics_metrics.description: computes a maximal set U of independent variables of an ideal given by a standard basis; returns an intvec v with v[i]=1 iff variable x(i) is independent. With second int argument returns a list of all maximal independent sets (or all those of the leading ideal that cannot be enlarged).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: indepSet(ideal expression) → intvec; indepSet(ideal expression,int) → list. Notes: U is independent for I iff I ∩ K[U] = (0); U maximal if dim(I)=#U. Examples show usage and interplay with eliminate and attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: insert
rubrics_metrics.description: inserts a new element into a list at the beginning, or after a specified position when called with three arguments (input list not modified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: insert(list expression, expression) or insert(list expression, expression, int). Type: list. Examples: list L=1,2; insert(L,4,2) yields [1,2,4]; insert(L,4) yields [4,1,2]. See delete and list sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: interpolation
rubrics_metrics.description: computes the reduced Groebner basis of the intersection of ideals l[1]^v[1],...,l[N]^v[N] using linear algebra; every ideal in l must be a maximal ideal of a point (variables = coordinates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: interpolation(list,intvec). Type: ideal. Requirements: polynomial ring over Zp or Q with global ordering. Example: constructs singular cubic through given points with multiplicities; shows subst and derivative checks. See diff, fglm, intersect, std, subst references.

rubrics_metrics.name: interred
rubrics_metrics.description: interreduces a set of polynomials/vectors: given f1,...,fn returns g1,...,gs with s≤n satisfying (f1,...,fn)=(g1,...,gs) and with distinct leading terms; also additional properties depending on global/local ordering and option(redSB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: interred(ideal expression) or interred(module expression). Type: same as input. Notes: defines L(g) and ecart(g)=deg(g)-deg(L(g)). Examples illustrate different orderings and results. Crossrefs: ideal, module, std.

rubrics_metrics.name: intersect
rubrics_metrics.description: computes the intersection of ideals or modules, optionally reporting the method (elimination/syzygies) if option prot enabled; optional last arg chooses Groebner algorithm ('std' or 'slimgb').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: intersect(expression list of ideal/module expression[, string alg]). Type: ideal or module. Examples show simple and nontrivial intersections and compare algorithms ('slimgb' vs default). See ideal, module, option.

rubrics_metrics.name: jacob
rubrics_metrics.description: computes the Jacobi ideal (for a polynomial), Jacobi matrix (for an ideal or module), generated by all partial derivatives of the input; arranges blocks diﬀ(MT,var(i)) horizontally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: jacob(poly|ideal|module). Type: ideal (poly), matrix (ideal), module (module). Examples show derivatives, matrix outputs, and repeated jacob calls. Crossrefs: diff, ideal, module, nvars.

rubrics_metrics.name: janet
rubrics_metrics.description: computes the Janet basis of the given ideal; with second argument 1 returns the standard basis. Works only with global orderings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: janet(ideal) or janet(ideal,int). Type: ideal. Example: cyclic 3 ideal yields a Janet basis with printed length. See groebner, ideal, std.

rubrics_metrics.name: jet
rubrics_metrics.description: truncates input (polynomial/vector/ideal/module) by deleting terms of degree greater than given integer; optional intvec provides weights; alternatives allow dividing by a polynomial/matrix (coefficient must be from a field).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple syntaxes (poly/vector/ideal/module with int, with optional intvec or divisor). Type: same as first arg. Examples: extracting homogeneous parts, absolute term, parts of maximal degree, truncation for series expansion 1/(1+x) up to degree 5. Crossrefs: deg, ideal, int, intvec, module, poly, vector.

rubrics_metrics.name: kbase
rubrics_metrics.description: computes a vector space basis (monomials) of the quotient ring by an ideal (or free module by a module) when finite dimensional and input is a standard basis; with second arg returns basis monomials of a given degree; if attribute isHomog present it's used as module weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: kbase(ideal/module) or kbase(ideal/module,int). Type: same as input. Note: if input is not standard basis the leading terms are used and result may be meaningless. Examples show outputs for finite and infinite quotients (degree-limited basis).

rubrics_metrics.name: kernel
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the kernel ideal of a given map; second argument must be a map from the basering to the given ring (or an ideal defining such a map).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: kernel(ring name, map name) or preimage(ring name, ideal expression). Type: ideal. Example demonstrates kernel(r,f) returning w. Crossrefs: alg kernel, hom kernel, ideal, map, modulo, preimage, ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: kill
rubrics_metrics.description: deletes objects (names) from the current session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: kill name or kill list of names. Type: none. Example: kill i,r removes variable i; subsequent reference to i gives undefined error. Crossrefs: defined, general lib.

rubrics_metrics.name: killattrib
rubrics_metrics.description: deletes attributes: either all attributes of an object or the specific attribute named by second argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: killattrib(name) or killattrib(name,string). Type: none. Examples: attrib(i,"isSB",1); killattrib(i,"isSB"); attrib(i) → no attributes. Crossrefs: attrib, option.

rubrics_metrics.name: koszul
rubrics_metrics.description: computes matrices of Koszul relations: koszul(d,n) for first n ring variables, koszul(d,id) for generators of an ideal, koszul(d,n,id) for first n generators of an ideal. These matrices form a complex (product of consecutive matrices is zero).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: koszul(int,int) / koszul(int,ideal) / koszul(int,int,ideal). Type: matrix. Examples show concrete matrices and that koszul(i,id)*koszul(i+1,id)=0. Crossrefs: int, matrix.

rubrics_metrics.name: laguerre
rubrics_metrics.description: computes all complex roots of a univariate polynomial using Laguerre's algorithm; second arg defines precision when ground field is Q; third arg (0,1,2) gives extra runs for improved results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: laguerre(poly,int,int). Type: list. Note: if ground field is complex numbers, list elements are type number; otherwise type string. Example roots printed. Crossrefs: none.

rubrics_metrics.name: lead
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the leading (initial) term(s) of a polynomial, vector, ideal generators, or module generators with respect to the monomial ordering. IN may be used instead of lead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: lead(poly|vector|ideal|module). Type: same as input. Examples show leading term for polynomial, vector, ideal, module. lead(0) → 0. Crossrefs: leadcoef, leadexp, leadmonom, ideal, module, poly, vector.

rubrics_metrics.name: leadcoef
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the leading (initial) coefficient of a polynomial or a vector with respect to the monomial ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: leadcoef(poly|vector). Type: number. Examples: leadcoef(f) → 1 for f=x2+y+z3; leadcoef([2*x^10,f]) → 2; leadcoef(0) → 0. Crossrefs: lead, leadexp, leadmonom.

rubrics_metrics.name: leadexp
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the exponent vector of the leading monomial of a polynomial or a vector; for vectors the last component is the index in the vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: leadexp(poly|vector). Type: intvec. Examples: leadexp(x2+y+z3) → 0,1,0; leadexp([2*x^10,f]) → 10,0,0,1; leadexp(0) → 0,0,0. Crossrefs: intvec, lead, leadcoef, leadmonom, monomial.

rubrics_metrics.name: leadmonom
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the leading monomial of a polynomial or vector as a polynomial/vector with coefficient 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: leadmonom(poly|vector). Type: same as input. Examples: for 2x2+3y+4z3 leadmonom(f) → y; leadmonom([0,2x10,f]) → [0,x10]; leadmonom(0) → 0. Crossrefs: lead, leadcoef, leadexp.

rubrics_metrics.name: LIB
rubrics_metrics.description: reads a library of procedures from a file and adds procedures to package Top and the package corresponding to the library; searches directories in SearchPath if filename not absolute or relative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: LIB string expression; Type: none. Note on standard.lib: loaded automatically unless Singular started with --no-stdlib. Example: LIB "inout.lib" loads and prints loaded message. Crossrefs: Loading a library, load, package, procedures, standard lib, system.

rubrics_metrics.name: lift
rubrics_metrics.description: computes a transformation matrix expressing generators of a submodule in terms of generators of a module: matrix(sm)*U = matrix(m)*T and module(sm*U)=module(matrix(m)*T); U stored in optional third argument (identity for polynomial rings). Gives warning if sm is not a submodule. Optional 4th arg selects Groebner algorithm ('std' or 'slimgb').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: lift(ideal,module[,matrix][,string]). Type: matrix. Example demonstrates matrix equality and difference zero. Crossrefs: division, liftstd, module, std, syz.

rubrics_metrics.name: liftstd
rubrics_metrics.description: returns a standard basis of an ideal or module and the transformation matrix from the given ideal/module to that standard basis; can also return syzygy module if third argument given; optional 4th arg selects Groebner algorithm ('std' or 'slimgb').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: liftstd(ideal/module,matrix[,module][,string]). Type: ideal or module. Examples show returned standard basis sm and matrix T with matrix(sm)-matrix(i)*T = 0. Crossrefs: division, lift, matrix, option, ring, std, syz.

rubrics_metrics.name: listvar
rubrics_metrics.description: lists all currently visible (user-defined) names with various filters: no args → all names except procedures in current namespace; with type/ring/name/all shows respective subsets; package argument can be Current, Top, or other package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: listvar([package][,type|ring name|name|all]). Type: none. Examples show output listing rings, polynomials, ideals, procedures, packages and how current basering is marked with *. Crossrefs: Names, Names in procedures, defined, names, package, type.

rubrics_metrics.name: lres
rubrics_metrics.description: computes a free resolution of an ideal using LaScala's algorithm: returns a minimal free resolution of R/I; if int arg k≠0 stops after k steps and returns list of modules Mi=module(Ai). Input ideal must be homogeneous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: lres(ideal,int). Type: resolution. Example: def L=lres(I,0); print(betti(L)); and access L[2] yields first syzygy module. Crossrefs: betti, fres, hres, ideal, int, minres, mres, res, sres, module.

rubrics_metrics.name: ludecomp
rubrics_metrics.description: computes the LU-decomposition of an (m x n) matrix A with entries from the ground field K: returns permutation P, lower triangular L (diagonal ones), and upper row echelon U with P*A=L*U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: ludecomp(matrix). Type: list (P,L,U). Requirement: matrix entries must be numbers from ground field. Example shows checking P* A - L*U = 0. Crossrefs: luinverse.

rubrics_metrics.name: luinverse
rubrics_metrics.description: computes the inverse of a matrix A if invertible; A can be provided directly or via its LU-decomposition P,L,U. Returns list L with either one entry 0 (not invertible) or [1,A^-1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: luinverse(matrix) or luinverse(matrix,P,L,U). Type: matrix (returned in list). Notes: Inverse exists iff U invertible; A^-1 = U^-1 * L^-1 * P. Warns for non-quadratic matrices. Example demonstrates checking A*L[2] = identity. Crossrefs: ludecomp.

rubrics_metrics.name: lusolve
rubrics_metrics.description: computes all solutions of a linear system A*x=b given the LU-decomposition of A (P,L,U) and b as m x 1; returns list Q with either one entry 0 (no solution) or [1,x,H] where x is any solution and columns of H span solution space of homogeneous system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: lusolve(P,L,U,b). Type: matrix (list result). Notes: if unique solution then H is 1x1 zero. Method checks dimension consistency and ground field requirement. Example demonstrates one-solution case and homogeneous solution basis. Crossrefs: ludecomp.

rubrics_metrics.name: max
rubrics_metrics.description: procedure from standard.lib that returns the maximum among arguments for types where > is defined (works for ints, intvecs, polynomials by leading monomial, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: max(i1,...,ik). Type: same as argument type. Examples: max(2,3)→3; max(intvec(1,2),intvec(0,1),intvec(1,1))→1,2; max(x+1,x^2+x)→x^2+x. See also min.

rubrics_metrics.name: maxideal
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the i-th power of the maximal ideal generated by all ring variables (maxideal(i)=1 for i<=0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: maxideal(int). Type: ideal. Example in ring r=32003,(x,y,z),dp; maxideal(2) returns list of standard monomials of degree 2 (z2,yz,y2,xz,xy,x2). Crossrefs: ideal, ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: memory
rubrics_metrics.description: returns memory management statistics: memory(0)=active (used) bytes; memory(1)=bytes allocated from OS; memory(2)=max bytes ever allocated during current session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: memory(int). Type: bigint. Note: to monitor memory during computations set option mem. Example includes a ReportMemoryUsage proc printing usage before/after killing objects. Crossrefs: option, system.

rubrics_metrics.name: min
rubrics_metrics.description: procedure from standard.lib (mirrors max): returns the minimum for arguments of a type for which '>' is defined. (Page contains copy-paste of max description but intended as min.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: min(i1,...,ik). Type: same as argument type. Examples analogous to max but returning minima. See also max.

rubrics_metrics.name: minbase
rubrics_metrics.description: returns a minimal set of generators of an ideal or module if the input is homogeneous or ordering is local. Not available over coefficient rings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: minbase(ideal/module). Type: same as input. Example: minbase on id4 returns list of monomial generators. Crossrefs: mstd.

rubrics_metrics.name: minor
rubrics_metrics.description: computes an ideal of minors of a matrix (detailed purpose and arguments begin on page but chunk truncated here).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax (partial): minor(matrix M,int mSize,[ideal I],[int k],[string algorithm],[int cachedP],[int cachedM]). Type: ideal. Purpose and full guidance truncated in this chunk.
